name: Gram
users: Me, across chat, phone, and desktop
card_line: A conversational meal logger and two-year fitness plan synced across devices.
page_subtitle: A fast conversational meal logger, a rules-driven Windows command center, and an Android sync app sharing one Google Drive event log.
time_to_build: Iterated over several months from initial plan synthesis to Drive sync, desktop analytics, and Android companion

snapshot.problem: My health history was split across five apps, and slow food logging or reactive calorie cuts broke consistency.
snapshot.what_i_built: A fast chat meal logger, a local Windows plan engine, and an Android widget sharing one immutable Google Drive log.
snapshot.result: Meal logging takes seconds, deterministic rules steer the two-year plan, and all three surfaces stay in sync.

problem: My nutrition, weight, lifting, and daily activity lived across Cronometer, FatSecret, JEFit, Hevy, and FitBit, with no single view to steer a long-term plan. When Cronometer went down during dinner, I logged food weights and photos in Gemini and realized conversational logging beat searching food databases. An early cloud reasoning agent took 30 to 60 seconds per entry, breaking kitchen use. I needed fast meal intake paired with a rules-driven plan that would not overreact to scale noise.

how_it_works.text: I fed three years of food, lifting, and weight exports plus injury notes into a frontier model to generate a governed two-year plan.
In the kitchen, I message Gram (a Grok Bot) with food weights or a photo; it returns calories, protein, and remaining targets in seconds.
Gram appends each meal as a versioned, immutable JSON event to a private Google Drive folder instead of overwriting a live file.
Physique Sync, a native Android app and home-screen widget, reads the Drive log into a verified cache and supports quick phone entries.
Physique Plan, my local Windows app, pulls Drive food events, Hevy workouts, and FitBit data into SQLite to track rolling averages.
Deterministic Python rules check weight trends, waist measurements, and lift signals, flagging stalls while refusing calorie changes on short windows.

decisions.reason: A deep-thinking cloud agent took 30 to 60 seconds per meal entry. Moving intake to a faster chat bot cut responses to seconds while keeping the same backend log.

decisions.decision: One immutable Google Drive event log.
decisions.reason: Chat and Android each append standalone JSON event files rather than editing a shared file, so I can swap chat agents or log from my phone without duplicates.
The chat agent only handles meal intake and macro math. Weight trends, maintenance estimates, and phase checks run in tested Python code requiring four-week windows before changing targets.

decisions.decision: Missing nutrients stay unknown, never zero.
decisions.reason: Partial meal entries leave blank carbs or fat unknown instead of zero, and the Android portion calculator refuses to suggest a serving when sync is stale or incomplete.

decisions.decision: Atomic phone uploads and local secrets.
decisions.reason: Android preallocates a Drive file ID, uploads exact bytes, and verifies readback so retries never duplicate entries. Desktop API keys stay encrypted locally using Windows DPAPI.

results.label: Replaced database search and 30 to 60 second reasoning lag with fast text or photo meal logging.
Consolidated Cronometer, FatSecret, JEFit, Hevy, and FitBit data into one shared history.
Plan rules require four-week trend windows and call out predictable month-three stalls.
Immutable Drive events let me swap chat agents or phone clients without losing history.

checks.label: 214 automated tests cover plan rules, Drive sync, Hevy workouts, FitBit imports, and nutrition math.
Verified that missing nutrients stay unknown instead of zero, and short weight windows never trigger reactive calorie cuts.
Replayed 315 real meal and weight logs across both the Windows and Android apps to confirm every daily total matched.
Tested interrupted phone uploads to confirm retries reuse the same Drive file and never double-log a meal.

next: Add fast voice and photo meal logging directly inside the standalone Android app so intake no longer requires opening a separate chat app.
Write standalone phone intake to the exact same immutable Google Drive event contract so desktop analytics and history need zero migration.
Automate background refreshes for the Android home-screen widget so daily calorie and protein rings stay current without tapping refresh.
